title: A finite separable field extension tensored with a field extension is reduced
statement: Let $L$ be a field, let $K'/L$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] ($K'$ a finite-dimensional $L$-vector space) which is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $E/L$ be any field extension. Then the ring $K'\otimes_LE$ (the tensor product of the $L$-algebras $K'$ and $E$, with multiplication $(a\otimes e)(a'\otimes e')=aa'\otimes ee'$ and unit $1\otimes1$) is reduced: it has no nonzero nilpotent elements.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, label line 10152), first paragraph, lines 10170-10182: $x_{r+1}$ with separable minimal polynomial $P$ over $k(x_1,\dots,x_r)$, the ring generated by $x_{r+1}$ with the single equation $P$ embeds into $F[T]/(P)$, 'Since $P$ is separable this is a finite product of fields'; here with $L=k(x_1,\dots,x_r)$, $K'=L(x_{r+1})$ and $E=F$ the fraction field; tag 030U verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (line 3961)
